findings.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:254 — SpawnProcess fails the new isinstance guard, so hung-worker recovery starts replacements without killing old workers, allowing concurrent workers and shared heartbeat updates on the same shards.

src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:254 — SpawnProcess fails the multiprocessing.Process isinstance check, so restarting a hung worker leaves it alive alongside its replacement and permits concurrent flushing of the same shards.

src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:340 — Breaking when the shared shutdown deadline expires skips termination of remaining workers, leaving stalled flushers running after join returns during rebalancing.

src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py:435 — The unbounded integer option permits negative counts that reach the process manager and fail with an opaque KeyError instead of enforcing a positive-count configuration boundary.

src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:61 — Worker lifecycle state is split across six parallel dictionaries keyed by process index, allowing future lifecycle changes to desynchronize shards, buffers, health, and restart counts.

src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:127 — The new _create_process_for_shard helper has no callers, leaving a dead shard-level restart path that can drift from the live process-level implementation.

src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:32 — The docstring promises one process per shard even when max_processes groups shards, leaving maintainers with an incorrect description of the configurable behavior.

src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:301 — Calling get_memory_info once per flusher buffer repeats Redis memory queries for shared services on every submit, so monitoring load grows with flusher process count.

src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:60 — A negative `--flusher-processes` value crashes startup while assigning shards, while zero silently bypasses the requested maximum and starts one worker per shard.

src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:254 — SpawnProcess fails this type check, so a hung flusher is replaced without being killed, leaving duplicate workers for its shards and exhausting process or Kafka resources.
src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:84 — If creation of a later worker fails, already-started workers are left running after SpanFlusher construction aborts.
src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:341 — Once the join deadline is exhausted, the loop skips terminating every remaining worker and can leave hung flushers running after shutdown returns.

src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:218 — The new per-process dead/hung-worker restart, shard metrics, and restart-limit branches have no tests, so a failed shard group can silently lose health recovery coverage.

tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py:85 — The process-limit test only asserts internal maps and never flushes spans from multiple partitions, so it would pass even if shared workers failed to produce buffered segments.

goldens.comment: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.

Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.

Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 254 in the diff, the code is `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process):` followed by `process.kill()`. The finding claims SpawnProcess fails this type check, but SpawnProcess is a subclass of multiprocessing.Process (it's created via `multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process`), so isinstance() would return True. The type annotation in the dict is `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess | threading.Thread`, and SpawnProcess inherits from Process. The isinstance check correctly distinguishes between Process objects (which have kill()) and Thread objects (which don't). The finding misunderstands Python's isinstance() behavior with inheritance.
